default: # OpenCityRecord MCP server OpenCityRecord gives your AI assistant the public record of local government: what was said at city council, planning commission, and county meetings, how each body voted, and what the city put in writing. Every answer links back to the source: the meeting page, the exact video timestamp, or the motion in the approved minutes. This repository holds connection configuration only. The server itself is a hosted service; there is nothing to install or run. | | | |---|---| | Endpoint | `https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp` (Streamable HTTP) | | Auth | OAuth 2.1 with Dynamic Client Registration: sign in with an OpenCityRecord account, no API key | | Registry | [`org.opencityrecord/opencity`](https://registry.modelcontextprotocol.io/v0.1/servers?search=org.opencityrecord) in the official MCP Registry | | Docs and sign-up | https://opencityrecord.org/mcp (the free account covers one city) | | Support | support@opencityrecord.org | ## What it covers - Meeting transcripts with jump-to-timestamp video links - Motions and roll-call votes from approved minutes, with dollar amounts - Agendas, minutes, staff reports, packets, ordinances, and resolutions - Current and former elected officials, with voting records - Issue and development-application timelines across meetings Coverage today is 340+ cities and counties in 14 states, mostly in Texas, Utah, California, Florida, Arizona, and New York, updated within hours of meetings being published. Elected officials are identified; members of the public, applicants, and city staff speaking at the mic are never named. All tools are read-only. ## Connect **Claude, ChatGPT, and other chat apps:** step-by-step instructions are at https://opencityrecord.org/mcp. **Claude Code** ```bash claude mcp add --transport http opencityrecord https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp ``` Then run `/mcp` in Claude Code to sign in. **Cursor** This repository is a Cursor plugin (`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` + `mcp.json`). To try it before it is in the Cursor Marketplace, clone it and add the folder under Cursor Settings → Plugins. Or add the server to `~/.cursor/mcp.json` yourself: ```json { "mcpServers": { "opencityrecord": { "url": "https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp" } } } ``` **Google Antigravity** This repository is an Antigravity plugin. Install it with the Antigravity CLI: ```bash agy plugin install https://github.com/OpenCityUSA/opencityrecord-mcp ``` Or add the server to `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json` yourself: ```json { "mcpServers": { "opencityrecord": { "serverUrl": "https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp" } } } ``` Antigravity handles the OAuth sign-in on first use. **Gemini CLI** This repository is also a Gemini CLI extension (`gemini-extension.json` + `GEMINI.md`): ```bash gemini extensions install https://github.com/OpenCityUSA/opencityrecord-mcp ``` Then run `/mcp auth opencityrecord` once to sign in. Or add the server to `~/.gemini/settings.json` yourself: ```json { "mcpServers": { "opencityrecord": { "httpUrl": "https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp", "oauth": { "enabled": true } } } } ``` **Gemini app** Once the OpenCityRecord connected app is published, type `@OpenCityRecord` followed by your question. Until then you can connect it yourself: open https://gemini.google.com/devmode, choose **+ Create new**, paste `https://mcp.opencityrecord.org/mcp` as the MCP Server URL, and pick **Dynamic Client Registration** under **Authentication**. ## Example questions - "What did the Lehi City Council decide in September?" - "Who is on the Salt Lake City council?" - "Which cities have voted on Flock Safety license-plate cameras, and what did they decide?" - "How did the short-term rental issue play out in Lehi?" - "How has Lehi council member Emily Lockhart voted since July?" ## Files | File | Used by | |---|---| | `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`, `mcp.json` | Cursor plugin | | `plugin.json`, `mcp_config.json` | Google Antigravity plugin | | `gemini-extension.json`, `GEMINI.md` | Gemini CLI extension (geminicli.com extensions gallery) | | `lhm.plugin.json` | LobeHub MCP Marketplace listing | ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE). The license covers the configuration in this repository, not the hosted service or its data.
